newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark breaks wedge, eyes fresh top.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark breaks wedge, eyes fresh top.

text.p: Dollar/mark got some help from dollar/Swiss on Friday, breaking out of a near two-week descending wedge formation and making a bid to retest multi-year highs reached earlier this month, technical analysts said.

A close in the high 1.73 area would keep the bullish trend on track for early next week, although an incremental move above the dollar's 39-month peak of 1.7420/25 marks would not necessarily guarantee further gains, according to chartists.
"I think dollar/Swiss is really dragging everything up today," said Martin Autotte, technical analyst at CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp in Montreal.
"We've broken the topside of a descending wedge formation in dollar/mark and the impulsive move that followed signals that we could see new highs early next week."
In late trade on Friday, the dollar was changing hands at 1.7395/05 marks and fetching 1.4540/45 Swiss francs.
A move through key resistance of 1.44 Swiss francs in oversease trade got the ball rolling for the dollar.
Darren Spain, global foreign exchange analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston, said his dollar/Swiss target for early next week was 1.4625/45.
He said 1.4625 was the June high for the rate, while the 1.4645 area represented downtrend resistance connecting highs since March.
Spain also predicted good upside potential for dollar/mark next week, but questioned whether a poke to fresh peaks would necessarily bode well for the rate.
"Dollar/mark is not as clear cut as dollar/Swiss because dollar/mark has a habit of making minor new highs and then not sustaining them," Spain said.
In dollar/yen, which was dragged higher by dollar/Europe on Friday, chartists saw room for a retest of key resistance at 115.70.
The dollar's ability to get through this tough barrier would determine its direction over the course of the coming week, they said.
